Album behavior on iPad (iOS/iPadOS)
- Do albums move or copy photos? They don’t move photos. An album is a collection that points to photos you already have in your Library. The originals stay in All Photos (and in any other albums you’ve added them to).
- If you accidentally remove a photo from an album, does it delete the photo? Not when you choose “Remove from Album.” It just takes the photo out of that album, but it stays in your main library. If you delete a photo from the library itself, it goes to Recently Deleted.
- Undo if you’ve made a mistake: In many apps you can shake the iPad to bring up an Undo option, or use the Edit/Undo controls in the app. For album changes specifically, there isn’t a universal “undo album addition” button, but you can easily re-add photos to an album or remove them again without affecting the originals. If you accidentally delete a photo from the library, you can recover it from Recently Deleted within 30 days.

How to manage and undo in Photos (quick reminders)
- Create an album: Photos > Albums > + New Album > name > Add Photos. The photos stay in All Photos.
- Remove from an album: Open the album > Select > Remove from Album. The photos stay in All Photos.
- Delete from library: In Photos, choose a photo > Delete. It goes to Recently Deleted (30 days to recover).
- Recover from Recently Deleted: Albums > Recently Deleted > select photos > Recover.

Backups and cloud storage: what’s actually saving
- iCloud Photos (cloud sync of your library): If this is on, photos you take or save to Photos on the iPad are uploaded to iCloud and appear on any other device signed in with your Apple ID and with iCloud Photos enabled.
- iCloud Backup (device-level backup): This backs up the whole iPad (settings, apps, data) to iCloud so you can restore the entire device if you get a new iPad or reset this one. It’s separate from iCloud Photos.
- Regular backups are good, but you want both: iCloud Photos for ongoing cloud copies of your photos, and iCloud Backup (or a computer backup) as a safety net for the whole device.

- Check iCloud Backup (device backup)
  - Settings > [your name] > iCloud > iCloud Backup.
  - Make sure it’s ON.
  - Tap Back Up Now to run a manual backup. After it finishes, you’ll see the date/time of the last successful backup.
  - If you don’t see a recent backup, check that there’s enough iCloud storage (Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Manage Storage).
- Quick sanity checks

- A practical test: Take a new photo or two, make sure you can see them in All Photos, and then check on the iPad later (or on iCloud.com) to confirm they’re there. If you see them on both devices, you’re effectively in sync.
